**Page:** Population and household estimates, Wales — https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/populationandmigration/populationestimates/bulletins/populationandhouseholdestimateswales/census2021

**Evidence**  
- “There were **1,347,100 households** in Wales on Census Day, which is a **3.4 % increase (44,400 more households)** on the **1,302,676 households in 2011**.”  
- “All but three local authorities in Wales saw an **increase in the number of households** compared with 2011. The local authorities that saw the highest increases were **Newport (8.1% increase)**, **the Vale of Glamorgan (7.5% increase)** and **Monmouthshire (7.0% increase)**.”  
- “The areas where there were decreases in the number of households were **Gwynedd (2.6% decrease)**, **Ceredigion (2.1% decrease)** and **Blaenau Gwent (0.4% decrease)**.”

**Coverage**  
- **Household counts** for Wales as a whole (2011 and 2021) – complete.  
- **Local‑authority household change rates** for three authorities with largest increases and three with decreases – partial, not a full list of all 22 Welsh local authorities.  
- The statement that “All but three local authorities saw an increase” gives a binary condition for the other authorities but no specific names or rates.

**Missing**  
- Names, household counts, or percentage changes for the 19 local authorities that are not listed as having the biggest increases or as having decreases.  
- Mid‑year 2021 population or household figures at the local‑authority level.  
- Population figures for 2021 mid‑year and 2022 mid‑year at the local‑authority level, especially for sub‑age group 25‑44.  
- Regional classification (e.g., North Wales vs. other regions).  
- Any data on whether local authorities saw an overall decrease in households; only the exception case (decreases) is explicitly named.

**Next links**  
1. **Page for local‑authority household estimates** – https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/populationandmigration/populationestimates/datasets/populationandhouseholdestimateswalescensus2021 (provides detailed household counts for each local authority).  
2. **Interactive figure of household changes by local authority** – https://www.ons.gov.uk/visualisations/dvc1915/fig6 (contains a map/table of household changes, including names and percentages).  
3. **Mid‑year population estimates for Wales** – https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/populationandmigration/populationestimates/bulletins/mid2021 (potential source for 2021 mid‑year population at local‑authority level).  
4. **Annual mid‑year population estimates 2022** – https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/populationandmigration/populationestimates/bulletins/mid2022 (potential source for 2022 mid‑year data).  
5. **Age‑specific population datasets** – https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/populationandmigration/populationestimates/datasets/populationandhouseholdestimateswalescensus2021 (could be filtered for age group 25‑44).

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Dataset ID 82d9faea-b515-41cd-aedb-8f4594f66ce5

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation

Designation Accredited official statistics

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Designation Accredited official statistics

Data source Mid-year population estimates

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Main information

Designation Accredited official statistics

Data provider Office for National Statistics (ONS)

Data source Mid-year population estimates

Dataset ID 82d9faea-b515-41cd-aedb-8f4594f66ce5

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Then we need 2021 data for 25-44 for each authority. We already have a link that is 2021 Merthyr only; we need 2021 for Torfaen and Monmouthshire. So we need two more links: 2021 Torfaen, 2021 Monmouthshire. That would be 3 links plus 2022 all authorities. That's 4. But only 2 child nodes left. Maybe better to get 2021 all authorities, 2022 all authorities. That's 2 links total. Then from those CSVs we can parse the values for Merthyr, Torfaen, Monmouthshire. Great.

Thus follow two pages: one with Year=Mid-year 2021&Age=25 to 44 ; second with Year=Mid-year 2022&Age=25 to 44 (no area filter). That will give all local authorities. We'll fetch both.

We have the 2021 URL partly: https://stats.gov.wales/en-GB/82d9faea-b515-41cd-aedb-8f4594f66ce5?format=csv&Year=Mid-year%202021&Age=25%20to%2044

Let's fetch that.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

## Overview

Summary of dataset and variables
This dataset provides population estimates for the local authorities in Wales, the English regions and the UK countries for the period from 1991 onwards by sex and single year of age.

It should be noted that for mid-2020 there are some definitional changes, particularly affecting the migration components, compared with mid-2019 population estimates data and it is advised users read the Quality and Methodology Information section on the Office for National Statistics website.

For Wales, England and Northern Ireland, the mid-2021 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2021 censuses for these countries. For Scotland, the census was moved to 2022. The mid-2022 population estimates are the first population estimates to be based on the 2022 Census for Scotland.

On 23 November 2023, the data set from 2012 to 2020 for Wales and England were rebased to be consistent with the results of Census 2021. Northern Ireland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 29 June 2023. Scotland published rebased 2012 to 2020 data on 9 July 2024.

On 29 July 2026 estimates for mid-2022, mid-2023 and mid-2024 were revised by the ONS to account for updated estimates of international migration for Wales and England.

Internal migration estimates for mid-2023 have been produced using a different method to previous years, following a change to the variables available in the Higher Education Statistics Agency data.

Data collection or calculation
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on how the data are calculated can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.

Statistical quality
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) publish mid-year population estimates for Wales and England as a whole. Further information on statistical quality can be found on the ONS' website. A link can be found in the weblink section.
